ir.name: loss_pairwise_advantage_logsigmoid_weighted
ir.intuition: Repaired to improve novelty and leverage a different signal by switching from delta_rank to advantage_gap as the quality signal. This shifts the loss focus from rank differences to modeled advantage, providing a fresh perspective on preference learning. The margin is defined as the difference between winning and losing log probabilities, scaled by advantage_gap, then passed through a logsigmoid link and weighted by sample weight and advantage magnitude. This design maintains the pairwise logsigmoid paradigm but uses a different, supported signal and weighting scheme to ensure distinctiveness and effectiveness.
ir.pseudocode:
lpw = batch['log_prob_w']
lpl = batch['log_prob_l']
adv_gap = batch['advantage_gap']
weight = batch.get('weight', None)
x = ops.mul(ops.sub(lpw, lpl), adv_gap)
losses = ops.neg(ops.logsigmoid(x))
weighted_losses = ops.mul(losses, adv_gap)
if weight is not None:
    weighted_losses = ops.mul(weighted_losses, weight)
return ops.sum(weighted_losses)
ir.code:
def generated_loss(batch, model_output, extra):
    lpw = batch['log_prob_w']
    lpl = batch['log_prob_l']
    adv_gap = batch['advantage_gap']
    weight = batch.get('weight', None)
    margin = ops.sub(lpw, lpl)
    x = ops.mul(margin, adv_gap)
    losses = ops.neg(ops.logsigmoid(x))
    weighted_losses = ops.mul(losses, adv_gap)
    if weight is not None:
        weighted_losses = ops.mul(weighted_losses, weight)
    return ops.sum(weighted_losses)
ir.theoretical_basis: Using advantage_gap as a signal emphasizes the model's predicted benefit of the winning sequence over the losing one, which aligns well with pairwise preference learning objectives. The logsigmoid link converts margins into probabilistic loss terms suitable for gradient-based optimization, while weighting by advantage_gap prioritizes pairs with stronger preference signals.
